messages.content: You extract lessons for an automated numerical-analysis lab from its own attempts. A lesson is a short rule with the conditions under which it applies. Never turn a detail of one attempt into a universal rule: cite the attempts that support each lesson by their labels. Answer with JSON only.

Target quad-d7: exact to degree 7 on the interval [-1, 1] with the fewest nodes. Certificate: quadrature_exactness; entry point rule().
Task prompt:
---
Task: construct a quadrature rule on the interval [-1, 1] that integrates every polynomial of total degree at most 7 exactly, with as few nodes as possible.

Write one complete Python file that defines

    def rule():
        ...
        return nodes, weights

where nodes is a list of floats x_i in [-1, 1] and weights is a list of floats of the same length, so that
    int_{-1}^{1} p(x) dx = sum_i weights[i] * p(nodes[i])
for every polynomial p of degree <= 7. The judge applies the rule to every monomial of degree <= 7 and to random polynomials; the largest error must be below 1e-9. The score is the number of nodes: fewer is better.

Rules: use plain Python and NumPy arithmetic only (numpy.linalg is allowed). Library quadrature, root-finding and optimisation functions are forbidden and fail the attempt: numpy.polynomial, scipy.integrate, scipy.optimize, scipy.special, scipy.interpolate, sympy, mpmath. No files, no network, no printing. Reply with exactly one ```python code block containing the whole file.
---

Active lessons:
1. id=les_662eac2a09f9 level=approach evidence=observed support=4: [approach] Use Gauss–Legendre construction (n-point Golub–Welsch or root-finding on Legendre polynomial) to get minimal nodes for exactness degree 2n-1.; applies when: Target is exactness on [-1,1] for polynomials; You want minimal node count
2. id=les_61168926203b level=process evidence=observed support=3: [process] Always self-verify the rule by testing all monomials up to target degree and checking node/weight counts before submitting.; applies when: Target exactness degree is known; Numeric tolerance required (e.g. 1e-9)
3. id=les_6efe61d8509e level=process evidence=observed support=3: [process] Prefer symmetric constructions (mirror nodes, paired weights) to reduce roundoff risk and maintain positivity when integrand/domain symmetric.; applies when: Domain symmetric [-1,1]; Even/odd polynomial moments structure applies
4. id=les_780a770fd2c1 level=implementation evidence=observed support=3: [implementation] Do not import forbidden modules; implement Golub–Welsch with numpy.linalg.eigh or a local Newton for roots instead of numpy.polynomial or scipy functions.; applies when: Execution forbids numpy.polynomial.*, scipy.*, sympy, mpmath; Linear-algebra (numpy.linalg) is allowed
5. id=les_fffa6fcc66b1 level=implementation evidence=observed support=1: [implementation] Return lists of equal length: nodes and weights must match; mismatched lengths cause immediate failure.; applies when: Function must return nodes, weights; Judge enforces length consistency

Choose the one lesson most likely to raise the certified rate on this target, say why in one sentence, and write a concrete check to run on the candidate's returned value before it is submitted: a one-line description and a single Python expression over nodes (list of node coordinates), weights (list of floats), n (number of nodes) using only arithmetic, comparisons, abs, sum, min, max, len, sqrt, all, any, pi and list comprehensions (no powers, no imports, no attributes). Reply with JSON: {"lesson_id": "les_...", "why": "...", "check": {"description": "...", "expression": "..."}}
